outcome: Oracle has a researched connectivity topology for concrete source adapters so the system can reach required external/internal information through explicit, replaceable infrastructure seams; MCP is evaluated only as a source/capability adapter, not as an Oracle lifecycle or generic framework.
currentProblem: Current Oracle has two concrete readers injected by callers and no MCP path. After physical extraction, source connectivity needs an explicit topology that says where repository, application-artifact, and future concrete external adapters live, how identity/provenance is preserved, and which protocol concerns stay below application lifecycle.
constraints: Repository and application-artifact sources remain distinct where their identity/provenance semantics differ.
Adding connectivity must not create an Oracle agent loop, provider lifecycle, generic registry or background refresh system without evidence.
MCP, if used, is a protocol/source adapter below the Oracle/Application semantic boundary and owns no work/task lifecycle.
Every resolved input retains stable source identity/provenance sufficient for downstream evidence.
Source failures fail closed with exact requested source/path/ref context.
successCriteria: Research maps current repositoryReader and artifactReader into the extracted Oracle package with explicit adapter ownership.
A future concrete external/MCP-backed source has a bounded adapter contract and cannot inject lifecycle/acceptance authority.
Adapter topology preserves source identity/provenance and distinguishes external repository vs internal accepted application artifacts.
No generic provider registry is required to add one concrete adapter.
An end-to-end ingress path from declared application need to validated Worker context is specified with failure semantics.
